comments.author: kuzehanka
comments.story: Quake II RTX: Re-Engineering a Classic with Ray Tracing Effects on Vulkan
comments.why: Shows deep learning denoising that makes low-sample ray tracing usable.
comments.text: Deep learning denoiser. I don't know if NVIDIA came up with some marketing term for it. It's what allows RTX to produce meaningful images at all despite the renderer running at 0.5-2 samples per pixel which looks little better than random noise. I kind of assumed they'd call it DLDN because they called their deep learning supersampling DLSS. I guess not, go figure. [VIDEO]
